reports.source_excerpt_for_review:
Title: Astro's Playroom, PPSA01325, 01.905.000
Host: Arch Linux, RTX 5080 (NVIDIA 615.78), 31 GiB RAM, GCC 16.2.1

On `main` d31b57a4c it does not load: the title imports `libSceJobManager.prx` and does not ship it (#2476). With the changes below on top of `main` it gets through start-up and stops in the font code about 50 s in. Each one removed the stop next to it, in this order. None of the three PRs is specific to this title: the first is a system library any title that imports it and does not ship it needs, the second changes how every system library is linked on Linux, and the third is a recompiler case measured on hardware and covered by its own test.

- #3186, the library itself: the title loads.
- #3214: `sceLibcInternalHeapErrorReportForGame_nid_postfix not implemented` at 40 s. The title's libc was reporting heap damage done by the dynamic linker running on a 2 KiB fiber stack.
- #3222: `image descriptor is incompatible with the static runtime image interface: descriptor format 71`, a 2D `image_sample` on a 1D T#.
- Substitute fonts in `anyps5-fonts/` as `docs/user/USAGE.md` describes. Without them every `sceFontOpenFontSet` fails and the title asserts `Out of Global Heap Memory` with its heap half empty: it sizes a font surface from a width it never got and asks for 2 GiB.

Current stop, 4 of 4 runs: `sceFontWritingLineWritesOrder: writing attribute 250 is not modelled`. I have no source for what that attribute does on the console, so I have not implemented anything for it.

On screen, in the one run I captured with fonts in place: the window stays almost black, the frame counter in the window title stops at 120 around 30 s, and the title ends on the font error at about 48 s.

**Status: playable on Windows** with the patches below. It boots, reaches the menu, and plays with music and sound effects at a steady 60 FPS, with no flicker or crashes in my testing.

- Version: EU, `EP3495-PPSA21402`, game build 1.0.1o-FULL

| Music | #1038, streaming 16-bit PCM through appended waveform blocks (flag `0x2`) |

```diff
 void WaitForFlipRoom() override {

reports.source_excerpt_for_review:
I reproduced startup of lowbit's public PS5 DOOM homebrew with AnyPS5 on Windows. The guest executable reached its entry point, created a Vulkan window on an RTX 3060, and subsequently logged DOOM shareware initialization. The first AGC presentation frame failed and the port switched to its CPU scaler.

**Scope: startup and log observations only.** I have not visually verified rendering, tested movement/firing, heard the audio, or established sustained gameplay stability. The window-title FPS counter is not a gameplay benchmark. This is the homebrew port of classic DOOM, not a retail PS5 DOOM title.

### Existing work

This is an additional reproduction, not a first-run claim. I searched Discussions for DOOM and found no matching discussion, but the issue history already contains relevant results:

- #1578: LeandroLP23 reports ps5-doom running on Windows as an import-audit control.
- #1497: hikazey reports Linux gameplay and the same first-frame/CPU-scaler fallback; that thread also covers bundled libc shim binding and references #690 and #1529.
- #2433 is related PS4/PS5 container research. Container extraction alone does not establish PS4 runtime compatibility.

### Sample and build

- Public release: [lowbit/ps5-doom v1.1.1](https://github.com/lowbit/ps5-doom/releases/tag/v1.1.1), title PPSA99666.
- Corresponding source: commit ba6e305bd315828c0980ff93eb54e35c8ebf397b.
- Release ZIP SHA-256: 4d8e5b785b61696fbf1988c2d0d87c5c977734ff60b1ce11cc49134b0e711b5f.
- Reconstructed eboot ELF SHA-256: 62d4cfe60815afbbebbd1916eb6b08fa5bd53e36d3ced68d9b62a6488bb37378; it matches the digest recorded in the plaintext FSELF container.
- Windows, Ryzen 5 7600X, NVIDIA RTX 3060, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0.
- AnyPS5 upstream base: 025a911360a91b22fb316baf67c6b660dd42d736.

reports.source_title: Dreaming Sarah (PPSA02929) on Windows: boots to first render, crashes in amdvlk64 on RX 6700 XT
reports.source_excerpt_for_review:
### Environment
* **OS:** Windows 11 Pro 23H2 (build 22631)
* **AnyPS5:** built from `main` `57f96fd`, WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 r7 (15.2.0posix-14.0.0-ucrt-r7), Ninja, Release, `BUILD_TESTING=ON`
* **Game/Executable:** Dreaming Sarah (`PPSA02929-app0/eboot.bin`)
* **GPU:** AMD Radeon RX 6700 XT (Navi 22, device 0x73df, Adrenalin 25.10.45.05, driver 32.0.21045.5002 dated 2026-08-16, Vulkan 1.4.315), the only Vulkan device, auto-selected

### Conversion

`relinker --windows eboot.bin game.exe` succeeds. 815 NID input references. The bundled `sce_module/libc.prx` converts as a guest module. One dumping-tool note: the dumper left decrypted ELF copies as `eboot.bin.esbak`/`libc.prx.esbak` beside the encrypted files, and the `.esbak` inside `sce_module/` is scanned as a second guest module, failing with `Ambiguous guest dependency name: libc.prx` (both files carry SONAME `libc.prx`). Moving the `.esbak` files out of the module directory is enough.

Import audit (exit 0): 553 unique imports, 918 references - 367 implemented, 16 stub, **0 absent**, 170 module (the title's own libc.prx). The 16 stubs are capture/diagnostics functions (`sceAgcDcb*`/`sceAgcAcb*` capture, `sceAgcDriverRequestCapture*`, backtrace/heap-report postfixes, `__tls_get_addr` postfix).

### Runtime

The title boots through the whole stack: ELF entry, guest threads, save data mount (`mount3` -> `/savedata0`), full Vulkan device init on the RX 6700 XT, shader disk cache creation, resource loading (language files, `media/error.flac` background load), render target allocation up to 14 MiB and texture creation (1280x720 storage images, 320x512/980x347/250x250 textures). It then crashes at the first real graphics submission:

```
FATAL: unhandled exception 0xc0000005 on thread 15024 ''
  rip 0x00007ffbeacdef34 amdvlk6

## Tested

- **Title:** Ghost of Yōtei, PPSA26344, v1.008
- **Host:**
  - Windows 11 Pro, Intel Core i9-11900H (Tiger Lake, 8 cores), 32 GB RAM, 32-64 GB page file.
  - NVIDIA RTX 3080 Laptop GPU 16 GB, driver 610.62.
  - Relinked with `--windows --to-intel`. Built with MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0.
- **Last update:** 2026-10-05. 24 of the 26 pull requests below are merged; #648 and #653 are open.

## Status

Not in game. With the pull requests below on `main`, the title:
- resolves all its imports (its own `libc.prx` included);
- reaches its entry point, starts its job threads and opens its `/app0/cache_ps5` files;
- allocates 13.5 GiB of direct memory and makes 835 fixed mappings up to 0xFC_0000_0000;
- creates its AudioOut2 graph: two 7.1.4 beds, 38 object ports, pad speaker and vibration;
- registers DCC display buffers, creates the Vulkan device and runs its first compute passes.

Its first frame submission (8440 dwords, ending in a FLIP) is accepted and starts executing. It then stops in the "Tiled Decals" compute pass (blocker A). No frame has been presented yet.

## Open blockers

| | Stop | Seen |
|---|---|---|
| A | `compute shader 0x80003aa700: GetImageResource dword 0 is not a valid runtime value`. The image descriptor is loaded from a descriptor table at an offset computed from the thread id inside a loop. | Every launch, a few seconds in |
| B | `[gpu] skipped draw: unsupported PA_CL_CLIP_CNTL flags (register 0x204 = 0x01080000)`. Draws are skipped; not fatal. | Every launch. Covered by #678 (merged) |
| C | Tessellation. The `tessellationAvailable=0` log line was printed before the feature was read (#687 (merged)); the device has it. The native LS/HS/DS path is not complete: no lowering of the HS/DS ring and LDS accesses, no tessellation

still does not reach gameplay, and the two walls that remain are a software-rasteriser device limit and a
memory ceiling — neither is a correctness bug in the emulator.

(General discussion of the title lives in #675; this thread is the Linux-facing update.)

**Latest `main` plus three *open* PRs stacked locally** — **#1940** (aperture — **mine**), **#757** and
**#758** (image/sampler tables and 64-bit table pointers — **@Celegans12**'s) — together with
**@pipodi93**'s fix for relocated shader headers.

- **None of those three PRs is merged upstream.** I merged them into a local test build. If you want the

## Status

**On the [`gta-v/testing`](https://github.com/MichonGoddijn231849/AnyPS5-fork/tree/gta-v/testing) branch** (based on `main` from before #639): in game on Windows. "Resume Story" starts the North Yankton prologue, which plays with rendering, reflections, music, speech, sound effects and the HUD working.

**On current `main`** (d70b8998, 2026-10-09): stops at boot. With the open pull requests under "Needed on current main" below it presents its first frames (the start screens), then stops on a T# read from a material table (bindless image tables, #1184). Getting it in game on `main` is what I am working on now.

![GTA V prologue, Performance mode](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MichonGoddijn231849/AnyPS5-fork/pr-assets/gta-prologue-performance.png)

| Graphics mode (`gta-v/testing`) | State |
|---|---|
| Performance | Playable, around 27-28 fps in the bank (was 20-23) |

### Status
**Playable, with warm shader caches.** On main 961b25fe with the PRs below, it boots, loads a game and plays, with no skipped draws. Standing in the hub it now sits at the 60 fps cap (p95 frame 16.7 ms) with pipelined draws from #1201 on (`APS5_PIPELINED_DRAWS=1`). That's the original executable with its 512 MiB upload pool, no patches.

The level-load crash from yesterday is gone on main: #2647 gives guest threads their host stack room back. The one catch left is that **it only boots when the shader caches are warm**. More on that below.

Some things worth knowing about how the game runs:
- It ships its own `libc.prx`, `libSceJobManager.prx`, `libSceNpCppWebApi.prx`, `libSceFontGsm.prx`, `libScePfs.prx` and FMOD (`libfmod.prx`, `libfmodstudio.prx`). All of them load as guest modules from `sce_module`.
- Its bundled libc replaces malloc with an mspace over 1 GiB of direct memory, mapped CPU-only (`3`).
- It maps 6784 MiB of GPU memory (`0x32`): a 512 MiB upload pool, a 6 GiB heap and another 128 MiB.
- The upload pool is the tricky part. The loader only frees it after a GPU fence, so anything that slows the fences down makes it overflow during startup. With everything below and warm caches, it peaks at 330-390 MiB out of 512.

You need an import budget of at least 6784 MiB, so either #290 or `APS5_HOST_IMPORT_MIB=8192`. I run with the env var, since #290 doesn't merge cleanly with current main.
